sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.8% a year from $22.7 billion in FY2016 to $31.7 billion in FY2025 [F1][F9][F198], while operating income grew faster at 5.8% [F199].
The window is a slow, regulated grind upward rather than a step change, with operating margin rising from 22.9% to 27.2% [F20][F28].
FY2022 was the sharpest revenue inflection, up 17.1% [D239], driven by rate cases, favorable weather and volumes [P26][P34].
FY2020 was the low point, with net income down 63.3% [D157] on coal-ash settlement impairments and pandemic volume losses [P60].
Electric Utilities and Infrastructure supplied 90.9% of FY2025 revenue [D541] and contributed 3.6pp of the 5.6% growth [D543][D358].
Residential electric was the largest single driver, at 43.3% of revenue [D774] and 2.8pp of FY2025 growth [D776].
Gas Utilities and Infrastructure added 2.0pp in FY2025 [D566], with Piedmont Natural Gas up 32.1% [D682].
Operating income grew 8.8% against 5.6% revenue growth in FY2025 [D359][D358], an incremental margin of 41.4% [D378].
Diluted EPS grew 8.2% a year against 9.7% net income growth [F202][F200], as the diluted share count rose from 691 million to 777 million [X106][X115].
FY2025 operating margin of 27.2% [F28] is the window high [D932], 4.3pp above the 22.9% median [D933].
The FY2025 margin rose 0.8pp [D370] as revenue growth outpaced operating-cost growth by 0.3pp [D379].
D&A rose to 24.3% of revenue in FY2025 from 21.4% in FY2024 [D341][D303], reflecting a growing asset base [P12].
Net margin of 15.7% [F47] sits 11.5pp below operating margin [D967], as interest expense reached $3.6 billion [X63].
Interest expense rose on higher outstanding debt balances and interest rates [P10], and the effective tax rate was 11.2% [D345].
Operating cash flow of $12.3 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025 [F77][D346], near the 2.59x window median [D958].
Free cash flow was negative $1.69 billion [F97], a -5.3% margin [D343], against a -5.8% window median [D939].
Capex of $14.0 billion was 44.2% of revenue [F87][D342] and 1.82x D&A [D348].
FY2022 conversion fell to 20.7% of revenue [D224] as rising fuel costs created undercollections that increased borrowings [P36].
Net debt reached $89.6 billion in FY2025 [D352], 282.3% of revenue [D353], with cash of just $245 million [F137].
That net-debt ratio is deeper than the utilities peer median net-debt ratio of 235.4% of revenue [D969], at the 33rd percentile of three peers [D968].
Total debt grew 6.6% in FY2025 [D376], with $11.9 billion issued against $5.7 billion repaid [X133][X143].
Return on average equity of 9.7% [D357] trails the 12.6% peer median [D956], at the 0th percentile of four peers [D955].
The current ratio fell to 0.55x in FY2025 [F177], the window low [D943], as current liabilities rose 8.7% [D369].
Cash covers only 0.1 years of the latest free-cash-flow burn [D356], leaving little standalone liquidity buffer.
Net debt has risen nine consecutive years to $89.6 billion [D14][D352], funding a capex programme that keeps free cash flow negative.
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 [D269][D309][D347], so earnings are not converting to distributable cash.
FY2021 operating expenses, pretax income and tax were later restated [X29][X69][X79], so FY2021 comparisons carry a basis caveat.
Operating margin: a print below the 22.9% window median [D933] in the FY2026 10-K would reverse the FY2025 high of 27.2% [D932].
Free cash flow margin: a move above the -5.8% window median [D939] toward the 0.2% FY2024 high [D938] would confirm capex is peaking.
Current ratio: recovery above the 0.66x window median [D945] would ease the liquidity flag set by the 0.55x FY2025 level [F177].
